Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

RdistNN 0.1.0.9003 (development version)

  • Use ordered compensated Mahalanobis projections so scalar and batch targets retain the same cancellation residuals across compiled and fallback engines.
  • Recover cancellation-sensitive covariance cross terms with compensated products and mean-subtraction residuals; test weight mass using the portable reduction.
  • Preserve scalar tuning sensitivity sweeps across optional return fields for NP, CATE, paired-ratio and CLATE fits with a manually chosen kernel order.
  • Retain custom tuning in experimental moment plots and clarify the original-unit Mahalanobis rank cutoff, with independent extreme-scale regression references.
  • Split shared input resolution, tuning schemas, grid evaluation and jackknife orchestration into dedicated modules while preserving public interfaces and numerical calculations. Remove unused duplicate helpers.
  • Strengthen cached-grid target and uncertainty alignment tests. Reorganize regression suites by behavior and improve fixture-state cleanup.
  • Check unique package-level helper ownership, candidate-file hygiene, generated Rd/namespace/Rcpp drift, and mirrored native headers. Keep the Stata companion on the same development version and refresh the documentation entry points.

RdistNN 0.1.0.9002 (earlier development snapshot)

  • Stabilize mixed-sign, large-offset jackknife signals and ordinary SD/covariance centering without dropping represented tails. Share portable exact rank-table recurrences across C++, R and Mata, including subnormal-tail safeguards.

  • Preserve data-frame selectors in NP/TDNN/CATE prediction, compute requested neighbors independently of SEs, and honor scalar tuning/uncertainty controls. Make NP/CATE tidy extraction grid-aware and name CATE coefficients by target.

  • Reject unrepresentable clipping intervals and partial AIPW nuisance inputs; support one-dimensional Mahalanobis geometry and stable signed-zero ties. Clarify Robinson propensity sensitivity and estimator-specific covariance/LOO contracts.

  • Retain resolved fitted geometry across NP/TDNN, CATE and paired-ratio/CLATE prediction. Preserve legacy geometry-refitting LOO inference. Compensate pure subset-score sums consistently in scalar, native and R evaluation.

  • Share an explicit compensated weighted-CDF boundary rule with Stata; keep selected observations exact across engines. Recover finite physical radii and weighted outcome SDs when intermediate squares overflow or underflow.

  • Reject fractional weight controls and conflicting core input routes; mark orders above n infeasible even for point-only grids. Honor normalize=FALSE in asymptotic DNN wrappers and correct TDNN zero-weight documentation.

  • Share compensated rank-weight normalization and weighted signal means across native and R paths. Retain correction state through prefix/suffix deletion merges, reuse the existing working-buffer budget, and align estimator, candidate and saved-prediction calculations with the Stata companion.

  • Fit Mahalanobis whitening factors directly from the centered training design with an explicit singular-value rank cutoff shared with Stata. Retain resolvable near-collinear directions, reuse C++/R L2 norms after projection, and preserve legacy saved inverse contexts.

  • Centralize covariance centering, binary range normalization and symmetric assembly across jackknife, NP/TDNN, paired-ratio and moment-covariance paths. Recover representable extreme variances; report unrepresentable nonzero variances as rescaling errors, or existing paired-ratio failure statuses.

  • Recover finite fitted SD scales and scaled L1 differences after intermediate overflow or underflow; reject nonfinite fitted scales before clamping. NP/TDNN prediction standard errors now compute marginal variances without allocating a full covariance matrix for the prediction grid.

  • Stabilize close-order TDNN coefficients with log1p/expm1, retain small asymptotic Beta-increment weights with direct tail probabilities, and recover representable extreme L2 norms through scaled sum-of-squares evaluation. Share the calculations across affected native and fallback paths and retain ordinary-input tie ordering and fitted geometry.

  • Align R L1/L2 distance fallbacks with compiled subtraction, scaling and coordinate accumulation order, preserving stable ranks near numerical ties and small differences at large coordinate offsets. Scaled evaluation reuses fitted scales with the supplied training matrix in both engine modes.

  • Add summary(), coef(), confint(), vcov() and saved-fit predict() methods for single- and two-scale NP regression, using retained training state and full common-deletion target covariance. NP, CATE and paired-ratio prediction share target validation; tabular covariate selectors retain resolved names so reordered prediction columns remain aligned.

  • Promote supplied-prediction conditional LATE and ordinary paired-signal ratios to supported workflows, including their shared reporting, diagnostics, plots and frozen-model reuse. Pointwise inference conditions are unchanged; ratio confidence-set inversion, PLQR and local IV-GMM remain experimental.

  • Advanced the shared development version to 0.1.0.9001 and documented local development branches, reviewed production PRs and R/Stata parity expectations.

  • Stabilized frozen-score jackknife calculations with target-specific, support-aware numerical centering across compiled, R, fast and explicit deletion paths. Zero-weight outliers no longer manufacture variance in locally constant signals. Exact and asymptotic weight rules are unchanged.

  • Reworked the README for package users, with current installation guidance, executable CATE, regression and CLATE examples, and shared reporting and plotting documentation. Updated the website reference descriptions and added contributor navigation.

  • Aligned CLATE and generic affine ratios with exact/asymptotic single-scale DNN, general k, normalization, tuning grids and candidate views. Prediction and diagnostics retain the chosen weights and frozen paired signals.

  • Standardized ratio summaries on the CATE coefficient-table schema, retaining component uncertainty and target statuses in separate fields. Added CATE-style estimate, weight, instrument-overlap, paired-score influence, tuning and dashboard plots, including plot() and ggplot2::autoplot() dispatch. Shared builders and rank-weight construction support both methods; TDNN remains separate NP-regression functionality.

  • Added experimental conditional LATE from supplied nuisance predictions with clate_dnn(), iv_augmented_signals() and the generic affine_ratio_dnn(). Both input formats retain paired components, covariance scales and explicit zero/negative-denominator statuses. Reporting, prediction and diagnostics reuse frozen signals; nuisance learning remains external.

  • Added ratio_confidence_set() with bounded, singleton, ray, half-line, all-real, empty and unresolved numerical results, plus a bounded clate_demo_data() benchmark and internal ridge-series reference adapter. New guides explain the estimand, covariance and pointwise inference scope.

  • Added independent subset/deletion references, signal identities, interface and validation tests, R/compiled parity, ridge refits and confidence-set geometry/rescaling tests. Hardened single-observation rank shapes, empty CLATE/ratio inputs and near-one confidence quantiles.

  • Replaced the superseded CATE and IV paper launchers with the current affine simulation and SIPP workflows. The bundle pins unchanged paper scientific source, all four accepted production configurations, and compressed evidence.

  • Added portable evidence rendering and validation runs, Linux measured production launches with resume checks, and SIPP full-fit/OOB/held-out replication with frozen-score and localization diagnostics.

  • Updated the replication article and package guidance to distinguish the current study from general simulation APIs. Accepted evidence regenerates all 21 manuscript tables and six PDF figures without refitting.

RdistNN 0.1.0

Initial public release scope

  • Refocused onboarding, package metadata, and the documentation site on CATE and nonparametric regression, with executable examples of both input formats, tuning, diagnostics, and the methods each result class supports.
  • Marked all PLQR functionality as experimental in help pages and articles, and grouped its estimator, scores, demos, inference methods, and specialized plots in the experimental reference section. PLQR continues to evaluate moments at supplied coefficients without solving for local coefficients.
  • Added contributor guidance, a source-package release checklist, and website announcement copy. This polish does not change estimator behavior or APIs.

Paper tuning defaults

  • tuning_dnn_paper() now uses the paper’s finite-sample default lambda = 0.4 and sensitivity grid c(0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.75), while preserving s(lambda) = floor(lambda * n^((kx + 1)/(kx + 2))) and all explicit tuning overrides.

Pre-release documentation and metadata

  • Added a notation and package-conventions vignette that maps public arguments and fitted-object fields to the companion papers, distinguishes effective local scale from physical support, and separates PLQR moment diagnostics from coefficient-level sandwich inference.
  • Corrected the np_dnn(), cate_dnn(), plqr_dnn(), and gmm_dnn() help pages so their automatic-order formula includes the finite-sample lambda = 0.4 multiplier used by the implementation.
  • Added the CATE inference contract to the README and command help: orthogonality controls first-order population nuisance drift, while same-sample reuse separately requires the paper’s nuisance-rate and full-state stability conditions.
  • Added the current paper link, repository and issue-tracker metadata, and explicit build exclusions for local check, archive, and rendered-README outputs.
  • Expanded release CI to run on default-branch pushes and to cover both Apple Silicon and Intel macOS alongside Windows and Linux. Clarified that OpenMP is optional at runtime but source installation still requires C++17.
  • Added options(RdistNN.use_compiled = FALSE) as a single switch for forcing supported R distance, score, and jackknife fallbacks, with compiled/fallback parity tests in the cross-platform matrix.
  • Removed local agent settings and paper PDF snapshots from version control, eliminated the dormant CI log-commit path, tightened default workflow permissions, and added a repository-hygiene guard for generated artifacts and finite artifact retention.

Theory-facing CATE simulation diagnostics

  • User-facing diagnostics(cate_result) now reuses the paper-simulation definitions for the ordinary-Euclidean 90-percent weight-mass radius, normalized treated/control arm ESS, and top-five absolute weighted score-contribution share, with explicit availability fields.
  • The CATE simulation now decomposes DNN error into realized localized-branch drift and estimator remainder, and records the corresponding root-effective- sample-size standardized drift.
  • Weight-based simulation rows now report a physical 90-percent-mass radius, treated and control effective sample sizes, score-contribution concentration, and the studentized error. summarise_sim_results() adds finite-sample studentized quantiles, skewness, excess kurtosis, and support summaries.
  • Integrated tuning-grid rows compute these diagnostics separately for every candidate while retaining shared-draw and shared-fitted-state parity.

PLQR jackknife-meat inference, supplied-theta semantics, and plot defaults

  • plqr_dnn() gains theta_meat = c("analytic", "jackknife"): with "jackknife", the full delete-1 jackknife covariance of the localized vector moment (moment_vcov) is used as the coefficient-sandwich meat with the density-backed bread. meta$theta_meat_method records the route; design note 15 now carries the full route table.
  • Supplied-theta semantics are explicit across the PLQR S3 methods: summary() prints theta_source and suppresses statistic/p.value for supplied evaluation values; coef(), confint(), and predict() attach a theta_source attribute and document that current fits repeat the supplied theta_eval.
  • PLQR estimate plots default to moment coordinates: plot_data_estimates()/plot_estimates() accept quantity = c("moment", "theta"), zero reference lines are drawn for moment plots only, and candidate-grid plots stay in moment coordinates.
  • .plqr_direct_sandwich() and the jackknife-meat route internally require normalized weight columns, failing clearly on rescaled or corrupted weight matrices.
  • PLQR Jacobian diagnostics rename density_min_weighted / density_max_weighted to density_min_support / density_max_support (they are support extrema) and add the weighted mean density_mean_weighted.
  • plqr_demo_data() now ships a true oracle threshold density: data$density_oracle and truth$density_fn, with the ALD error generator made density-continuous at the quantile (f(0) = 4 tau (1 - tau) / sigma; tau = 0.5 draws are unchanged). README and vignette examples use it instead of a hand-set constant.

Pre-public breaking cleanup (paper-notation alignment)

This pass deliberately breaks pre-release APIs so the first public version matches the conditional Z-estimation paper’s notation. No aliases for the old names are kept.

  • plqr_dnn(): renamed the shape-nuisance inputs q/q_col to g/g_col (the paper’s (g_0(U))) and the coefficient input beta to theta_eval. The result stores theta_eval (the supplied vector) instead of beta, and meta$theta_source = "supplied" records that no root solving was performed.
  • PLQR standard errors are no longer overloaded: coefficient-level direct-sandwich results live in theta_se/theta_vcov/theta_omega (previously se/vcov/omega), while the jackknife moment diagnostic lives in moment_se. meta$se_route was replaced by meta$theta_se_method and meta$moment_se_method.
  • Renamed the PLQR return extra "g" to "score" (stored as out$score), reserving g for the shape nuisance.
  • plqr_demo_data() now returns g_oracle, theta_true, g_fn, and g_x0 (previously q_oracle, beta_true, q_fn, q_x0).
  • Replaced the demo-bound plqr_moment() with the general plqr_score_matrix(data, y_col, D_cols, g_col, mD_cols, theta, tau).
  • score_plqr_component() gained an explicit y_col argument (the outcome column was hardcoded as "Y"), dropped the ignored compatibility-only k argument, and now uses g_col/theta notation throughout.
  • Renamed the rank-weight registry functions: register_rank() is now register_rank_weight(), get_rank() is get_rank_weight(), and rank_names() is rank_weight_names().
  • Direct PLQR coefficient inference now requires normalize = TRUE; fits combining density/density_col, se = TRUE, and normalize = FALSE error instead of returning scale-dependent standard errors.
  • Package Title/Description now lead with distributional nearest-neighbor inference for local conditional moment models rather than generalized U-statistics; the README labels the local IV-GMM layer as experimental companion functionality.
  • Renamed the paper-rule tuning constant from kappa to lambda to avoid a collision with the paper’s own use of kappa: tuning_dnn_paper(lambda =, lambda_grid =), candidate-table column lambda, candidate ids lambda_*, diagnostics column tuning_lambda_default, and the lambda column in sim_cate_* result and summary tables. No kappa alias is kept.
  • Removed the ignored compatibility-only k argument from score_cate_rho() and score_np_y(), matching the same cleanup in score_plqr_component().
  • Tuning-grid diagnostics payloads no longer carry the legacy duplicate top_share column; top5_weight_share is the single concentration field, and diagnostics() no longer accepts legacy payloads without it.
  • The experimental IV layer no longer aliases its target as tau: sim_iv_data()/iv_demo_data() drop tau_x0, truth$tau_fn, and the duplicate tau_oracle data column, keeping theta_x0/theta_fn/ theta_oracle only. tau remains reserved for the CATE target and the PLQR quantile level.
  • Exported-function documentation no longer names internal compiled rustat_* symbols; compiled fast paths are described generically.
  • Pruned the public namespace: the raw distance calculators and order helpers (dist_l1(), dist_l2(), dist_l1_scaled(), dist_l2_scaled(), order_by_l1(), order_by_l2(), order_by_l1_scaled(), order_by_l2_scaled()), the rank-to-weight plumbing (dnn_weights_*_full_from_ranks(), tdnn_rank_table_exact(), tdnn_rank_table_asymp()), and ord_to_ranks() are now internal. Use the distance_*() spec constructors and the rank_weight_*() / weights_*() layers instead; the internal implementations remain test-covered.

PLQR inference, prediction, and tuning-grid mode

  • Added the direct PLQR coefficient sandwich (density/density_col): plqr_dnn() now reports coefficient-level theta_se, theta_vcov, theta_omega, jacobian, score_covariance, and neff when a local conditional density is supplied, matching the direct J, S sandwich this estimator’s source theory specifies (see markdown_notes/design/15_plqr_variance_estimation_rationale.md). confint.plqr_result() and summary.plqr_result() report coefficient inference only through this route.
  • Added predict.plqr_result(), including coefficient-level se.fit/ interval = "confidence" support gated on the same direct-sandwich requirement.
  • Added tuning_mode = c("default", "grid") to cate_dnn(), np_dnn(), and plqr_dnn(): grid mode evaluates a tuning object’s feasible kernel- order candidates and attaches a tidy tuning_grid payload (candidates, estimates, diagnostics, meta), reusing cached ranks and rank-weight tables rather than refitting per candidate. See markdown_notes/design/14_integrated_tuning_grid_reuse.md.
  • Recorded, but deliberately did not build, a PLQR analogue of the sim-cate-*.R paper-simulation harness: the Cond_Z_Estimation paper has no PLQR numerical study to mirror, so a simulation harness would require inventing a DGP and comparator methods from scratch. Left as an explicit, flagged future-work item rather than undertaken speculatively.

Plotting layer (Phase 3)

  • autoplot()/plot() methods for plqr_result (zero-referenced moment facets with a theta_eval/tau subtitle) and gmm_result (coefficient facets with the model name); zero reference lines are now drawn for PLQR moments as well as CATE effects.
  • plot_conditioning() for PLQR fits: smallest Gram eigenvalue and log10 condition number across targets with caution/ill-conditioned guides at cond_limits.
  • plot_calibration() for PLQR fits: the weighted below-threshold share against the nominal tau with a normal reference band scaled by the local effective sample size; the indicator is stored on new fits and can be supplied as residuals otherwise.
  • plot_influence() for CATE fits: per-observation weighted score contributions against rank or distance, with the largest contributions labelled by observation index.
  • plot_tdnn_scales() overlays a TDNN fit with internal single-scale refits at s1 and s2.
  • plot_tuning() for np_result and cate_result: refits across the tuning grid’s candidate kernel orders (always including the fitted s) and plots estimate stability with the fitted order marked.
  • Fitted objects store the additional components these panels need: training data on np_dnn()/np_tdnn() fits, and the below-threshold indicator on plqr_dnn() fits.
  • Optional visual regression layer: vdiffr snapshots for the main panels, opt-in via the RDISTNN_VDIFFR=true environment variable so platform font differences cannot break CI.

Plotting layer (Phase 2)

  • plot_overlap() for CATE fits: type = "mass" draws the weighted treated/control mass per target with dotted share guides and shaded warning bands outside share_limits (violations reported in the caption); type = "propensity" draws weighted propensity densities at selected targets when observation-level propensities are available and a weighted q10-q90 summary otherwise. Inputs resolve through the documented precedence chain (stored fit components, then treatment/propensity arguments, then an actionable error).
  • autoplot()/plot() on diagnostics() frames: effective sample size (with the degenerate-weights guide at 0.9 n), maximum weight, and top-5 weight share faceted across targets.
  • plot_dashboard() for cate_result and np_result: patchwork composition with a metadata annotation (n, m, k, s with provenance, distance, jackknife type); unavailable panels are substituted (diagnostics facets replace a missing overlap panel) or dropped, and without patchwork the panels are returned as a named list with a message. patchwork joins Suggests.
  • Fitted np_dnn(), cate_dnn(), plqr_dnn(), and np_tdnn() objects record the jackknife type in meta$jackknife ("none" when se = FALSE).
  • New vignette visualising-fits walks from a CATE fit through the estimate, weight, overlap, and diagnostics panels to the dashboard and panel customisation.
  • The agent instruction files are excluded from the build, removing the long-standing top-level-files NOTE in R CMD check.

Plotting layer (Phase 1)

  • Added ggplot2-based plotting (ggplot2 is a suggested dependency; all entry points fail with an actionable message when it is missing): plot_estimates() draws point estimates with normal confidence bounds as a profile band (targets varying along one stored coordinate), a forest layout (small non-profile target sets, labelled from the stored coordinates), or pointranges, with an honesty caption carrying the median effective sample size and the kernel-order provenance on every panel; CATE panels add a dashed zero reference line and an opt-in shade_significant rug that marks intervals, never point estimates.
  • plot_weights() draws weight decay by rank (support-edge guide at n - s + 1, optional log scale), cumulative weight shares (0.5/0.9 guides and top-share markers), and the weight-vs-distance “effective kernel” view (rank-s radius guide); two-scale TDNN panels add a zero line for signed weights, and large target sets are subset to first/median-n_eff/last by default.
  • autoplot() (registered on ggplot2) and plot() methods for np_result and cate_result delegate to plot_estimates().
  • README gains a visualisation section with the CATE profile figure.

Plotting data layer (Phase 0)

  • Added the tidy data extractors behind the upcoming ggplot2-based plotting interface, with no plotting dependency: plot_data_estimates() (S3 generic with methods for np_result, cate_result, plqr_result, and gmm_result; TDNN fits dispatch through np_result) returns one row per target and coefficient with estimates, stored jackknife standard errors, and normal confidence bounds at a chosen level; plot_data_weights() returns per-(target, rank) weight profiles with cumulative shares and distances when stored; plot_data_diagnostics() returns the per-target diagnostics frame with an integer target_id aligned with the other extractors.
  • Maintainer architecture: markdown_notes/design/13_estimator_and_result_architecture.md.

Fitted objects store evaluation points

  • np_dnn(), cate_dnn(), plqr_dnn(), gmm_dnn(), and np_tdnn() result objects now include x0, the m x p matrix of evaluation points, with covariate column names propagated from the training data when the targets carry none. Profile plots need the target coordinates, which were previously not stored.

Breaking change: default kernel order s

  • np_dnn(), cate_dnn(), plqr_dnn(), and gmm_dnn() no longer default to s = 1L, which produced exactly uniform DNN weights and therefore no localization (every target point silently received the global weighted mean). When both s and tuning are omitted, s is now resolved from the paper undersmoothing rule tuning_dnn_paper(), s = floor(0.4 * n^((kx + 1)/(kx + 2))), matching the current default used by the Stata companion (cate_dnn.ado). The resolved rule is recorded in meta$tuning with source = "paper_default". Calls that passed s explicitly are unaffected.
  • All DNN and TDNN user wrappers now emit a warning when the computed weights are (near-)uniform (max effective sample size at least 0.9 * n, for example s = 1 or k = s), instead of silently returning an unlocalized fit.
  • Added tests/testthat/test-s-default-paper-rule.R, the s-analogue of the k = 1 documentation guardrail: it pins the default-s resolution for all four wrappers, the manual-s path, the degenerate-weight warning, and R/Stata default-formula agreement.
  • np_tdnn() still uses explicit s1/s2 defaults; a two-scale default rule is a separate follow-up.

Diagnostics and reporting

  • Added diagnostics() methods for np_dnn(), cate_dnn(), and plqr_dnn() fitted objects, including generic DNN weight/tuning summaries plus estimator-specific NP outcome, CATE overlap, and PLQR Gram conditioning diagnostics.
  • Added a diagnostics/reporting vignette and updated README, getting-started, conditional Z-estimation, kernel-order tuning, and pkgdown references to show the diagnostics workflow.

CI and package engineering

  • Added tools/ci/check_tests_declared_deps.R and a CI guard step to fail when tests/ uses pkg:: or pkg::: for undeclared packages.
  • Added tools/ci/check_pkgdown_reference_coverage.R and a CI guard step to fail when public man/*.Rd topics are missing from _pkgdown.yml reference contents.
  • Added tools/ci/check_generated_file_drift.R and a CI guard step to fail when generated files (NAMESPACE, R/RcppExports.R, src/RcppExports.cpp) are stale.
  • Added workflow .github/workflows/alignment-guardrails.yaml to run these guardrail checks on push and pull requests.

Dependency and docs alignment

  • Added tibble to Suggests for test-time namespace declarations.
  • Filled missing _pkgdown.yml reference entries for TDNN and Mahalanobis topics that were failing site checks.
